title: Handoff: Lighthouse ops log and action tracker - 2026-04-20
body:
OVERVIEW:
This is the lighthouse handoff for the overnight shift (20:00–08:00 PT). Primary focus: investigate and contain a sustained p99 latency uplift that started ~2026-04-20T00:50Z and recurred in three waves. No customer-facing SLA breach recorded, but several internal SLOs were nudged.

SUMMARY OF EVENTS (chronological):
- 00:50Z: Alerts triggered from 'inference-latency-p99' for hosted-api-us-west. Alert threshold crossed for 10m.
- 00:55Z: Pager duty ack by oncall (Samir). Quick sampling of traces showed increased tokenization time in the edge proxy service (proxy-tokenizer).
- 01:10Z: Mitigation attempt: increased proxy autoscaler target from 6->9 replicas (short-term). Latency improved slightly but not to baseline.
- 02:05Z: Second spike—correlated with a burst of large-sequence requests from a single API key (app-XXXXX). Rate-limiting rules not firing due to a missing header in requests; raised concern.
- 03:20Z: Escalation to infra (Asha) when cache hit-rate on prefix cache dropped to 18% from usual ~74%. Investigation pointed at a temporary key-sharding misalignment after a rollout earlier in the evening.
- 04:40Z: Rollback of the kernel-selection change (PR merged 2026-04-19 22:30) on a canary pool. Post-rollback metrics show return to baseline for that pool.
- 06:15Z: Final minor spike linked to backend quantization service (q-fuse) OOM restart; restart count = 2. Increased memory reservation in k8s manifest fixed overt restart, spike subsided by 06:45Z.

CUSTOMER IMPACT:
- No 5xx surge or visible errors in user traffic. A subset of high-throughput customers saw elevated tail latency for ~10–30 minutes per spike. Incident classified internal severity: Sev-N (impact to SLOs, not SLA).

ACTIONS TAKEN DURING SHIFT: (owner initials in parens)
- Scaled proxy-tokenizer horizontally to absorb burst (SP).
- Temporarily applied a stricter per-key burst limiter for the offending API key via WAF rule (SP, AP).
- Rolled back the kernel-selection change on canary pool (AP).
- Bumped q-fuse memory limits to reduce OOM restarts (LH).
- Opened SRE-3421 to track deeper root cause analysis on prefix cache sharding logic (LH).

PENDING ACTIONS / FOLLOW-UPS (action | owner | due):
- Add synthetic tests for prefix cache sharding across canary pools | Samir Patel | 2026-04-23
- Add logging to tokenization path to capture header shapes and durations (low perf overhead) | Claire Huang | 2026-04-22
- Harden rate-limiter to validate header presence and fallback | Asha Mehta | 2026-04-24
- Run a canary of kernel-selection change with a golden trace workload before next rollout | Platform Eng | 2026-04-25
- Update runbook: 'latency-tail-investigation' with new steps for prefix-cache mismatch and q-fuse OOM patterns | Liam O'Connor | 2026-04-23

NOTES FOR NEXT ON-CALL:
- Quick-check checklist (first 10 minutes after taking over):
  1) Check 'inference-latency-p99' dashboards (us-west and eu-west) and alert fabric.
  2) Inspect prefix-cache hit-rate aggregate and per-pool distribution. If any pool < 40%, consider pool-specific rollback.
  3) Verify proxy-tokenizer replica targets and cpu/memory saturation (recent autoscaler changes applied).
  4) Confirm q-fuse restart counts (kubectl get pods --restart-count).
  5) Look for any unusually large-sequence API keys with >100 requests/min in the last 30m.

- Temporary mitigations applied during the shift are recorded in SRE-3421 comments (link above) and in the infra incident channel (Slack link included). Please DO NOT remove temporary WAF rules without coordination.

RUNBOOK GAPS IDENTIFIED (need edits):
- Runbook 'latency-tail-investigation' lacks a section for 'kernel-selection' rollback playbook (exact commands and canary selectors).
- No explicit test harness for 'prefix-shard-mismatch' scenario—add a small deterministic test to run during deploys.
- q-fuse memory thresholds are currently based on historical defaults; need a reservation + limit re-evaluation tied to model size heuristics.

INCIDENT TIMELINE (short):
00:50Z Alert -> 00:55Z Ack -> 01:10Z Scale -> 02:05Z Identify bad API key burst -> 03:20Z Escalate for cache mismatch -> 04:40Z Canary rollback -> 06:15Z q-fuse OOM -> 06:45Z Resolved to baseline

KEY METRICS SNAPSHOT (from monitoring at 07:00Z):
- p99 latency (hosted-api-us-west): baseline 180ms -> peak 610ms -> current 195ms
- prefix-cache hit-rate: baseline 74% -> low 18% (affected pools) -> current 72%
- q-fuse pod restarts: 0 -> 2 -> 0 (after memory bump)

COMMUNICATIONS:
- Internal incident thread created in #sre-ops (link above).
- Notified Solutions Engs for the affected API key owner; they will follow up on abuse/third-party traffic patterns.

DECISION LOG / RATIONALE: 
- Chose to rollback the kernel-selection change on canary rather than cluster-wide because metrics indicated the canary pool diverged first and rollback had low blast radius.
- Applied temporary per-key limiter because repeated large-sequence bursts were the fastest mitigation to prevent repeated tail events while we fixed cache sharding.

DOCUMENTATION ATTACHED / EDITS NEEDED:
- Please append any debug traces and sample request headers to SRE-3421 (use the 'debug-traces' attachment field).
- Liam to draft runbook edits for 'kernel-selection rollback' and 'prefix-shard test' sections.

Handoff acceptance checklist (next on-call):
- I confirm clusters are at baseline: YES (at 07:00Z)
- Temporary mitigations documented: YES
- All critical follow-ups assigned: YES

Signed-off-by: Claire Huang (overnight lead)
